title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text: This guide describes how to integrate a new assessment model into the ASAR report workflow used in /Users/jim/_mymods/pollock/asar.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
1) Integration Targets
A model is considered “ASAR-ready” when you can produce:

A standardized model-results object named out_new saved as .rda.
Optional model-comparison tables and figures saved as ASAR-compatible .rda artifacts.
A report skeleton that renders with asar::create_template().

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
2) Required Data Contracts

2.1 out_new contract
out_new must be a data frame with the standard stockplotr/ASAR-style columns used by preamble.R (included in the report folder).
Minimum practical columns to populate correctly:

label (character)
estimate (numeric)
uncertainty (numeric or NA)
year (integer or NA)
era (character; use "time" for annual series rows)

The bridge script currently writes the full expected column set (33 columns), which is the recommended pattern for compatibility.


2.2 Labels expected by ASAR preamble
The current preamble logic computes report quantities from these label patterns:

fishing_mortality (time series, terminal year used for Fend)
f_msy or f_target (used for Ftarg)
biomass (terminal Bend)
biomass_msy or biomass_target (used for Btarg/Bmsy logic)
spawning_biomass (terminal SBend)
spawning_biomass_msy (optional, benchmark context)
catch (terminal total catch)
landings_observed (terminal total landings)
natural_mortality
beverton_holt_steepness
recruitment_unfished

If your model has different native names, map them to these labels in your parser.


2.3 Table .rda contract
Each table object must be saved as rda <- list(...) containing:

table (usually a flextable object)
cap (caption text)

Optional but recommended:

caption (duplicate of cap for portability)



2.4 Figure .rda contract
Each figure object must be saved as rda <- list(...) containing:

figure (ggplot or equivalent plot object)
cap (caption text)
alt_text (short accessibility description)

Optional but recommended:

caption (duplicate of cap)

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
3) Recommended File Layout
Within /Users/jim/_mymods/pollock/asar:

build_asar_bridge.R (or model-specific bridge script)
report/ (ASAR scaffold and std_output_*.rda)
tables/ (*_table.rda artifacts)
figures/ (*_figure.rda artifacts plus optional PNG/JPG)

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
section: 4) Step-by-Step Workflow For A New Model
text: 4) Step-by-Step Workflow For A New Model

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
section: Step 1: Build a parser from native output to out_new
text:
Step 1: Build a parser from native output to out_new
Create a parser function that:

Reads native model output files.
Extracts annual time series for biomass, spawning biomass, recruitment, fishing mortality, and catch/landings where available.
Extracts static benchmarks (e.g., Fmsy, Bmsy, steepness, R0 proxy).
Maps all extracted values to ASAR labels.

Use the same row-builder pattern as in:

/Users/jim/_mymods/pollock/asar/build_asar_bridge.R

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
Step 2: Save standardized output
Save to report folder as a stable filename, e.g.:

report/std_output_<model>.rda

where the saved object name is exactly out_new.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
Step 3: Generate tables and figures
At minimum, generate:

One terminal-status table.
One benchmark/reference table.
One time-series comparison figure (if multi-model context exists).

Save each as ASAR-compatible .rda objects in tables/ and figures/.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
section: Step 4: Build or refresh the ASAR template
text:
Step 4: Build or refresh the ASAR template
Run asar::create_template() with:

model_results pointing to your std_output_*.rda
tables_dir and figures_dir pointing to your artifact folders

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
Step 5: Render and validate
Render the report and confirm that:

Inline preamble values resolve (no missing object errors).
Tables and figures appear with captions.
References to @tbl-* and @fig-* resolve.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
5) QA Checklist (Use Every Time)

out_new file exists and loads.
Required labels are present.
estimate and uncertainty are numeric.
year values are valid for time-series rows.
Table .rda contains table and cap.
Figure .rda contains figure, cap, and alt_text.
support_files/cjfas.csl exists before render.
Quarto render succeeds without missing-resource errors.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
6) Common Failure Modes

Missing cap in .rda: ASAR chunk generation will reference ..._cap and fail.
Missing expected labels in out_new: preamble variables (e.g., Ftarg, SBend) become empty or ambiguous.
Non-numeric estimate: preamble calculations fail or return NA silently.
Multiple candidate rows for terminal/reference values: preamble may return vectors instead of scalars. Reduce to one value where appropriate.
Missing CSL/theme support files: render fails at pandoc stage.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
text:
7) Practical Pattern For Additional Models
For each new model, add a dedicated parser function and append its outputs to comparison artifacts, while keeping one canonical base-model out_new for report preamble quantities.
A stable pattern is:

parse_<model>_output()
to_out_new_<model>()
update_comparison_tables_figures()
render_asar_report()

This keeps model ingestion modular while preserving a single, predictable report build path.

title: Guide: Adopting New Models Into The ASAR Framework
section: Appendix A) Current Pollock Bridge Gaps (What Is Still Missing)
text:
Appendix A) Current Pollock Bridge Gaps (What Is Still Missing)
This appendix captures remaining gaps in the current pollock adoption (ebs_pollock -> asar) so new model integrations can avoid repeating them.

A.1 Report Portability Is Still Incomplete
Several report chunks still read inputs using machine-specific absolute paths. Examples include:

report/04b_assessment-results.qmd (pm.par path)
report/04e_assessment-projections.qmd (F40_t.rep path)
report/08_tables.qmd and report/09_figures.qmd (hard-coded tables/ and figures/ roots)

What is missing:

Parameterized/relative input paths across all report chapters.
A fully self-contained report build that can run outside the current local filesystem layout.



A.2 Figure Packaging Is Partial
build_asar_bridge.R currently writes one packaged comparison figure (model_timeseries_figure.rda) and two packaged tables, but most report figures are still direct static PNG references.
What is missing:

A full set of ASAR-style packaged figure artifacts (rda$figure, rda$cap, rda$alt_text) for key diagnostics (including BTS/ATS/AVO suites).
A single figure-generation path that does not rely on pre-existing copied PNGs.



A.3 Some out_new Mappings Need Model-Specific Validation
The pollock bridge currently uses pragmatic mappings that should be validated per model:

landings_observed is populated from catch_obs.
spawning_biomass_msy is populated from Bmsy in F40_t.rep.

What is missing:

Explicit confirmation that these mappings are semantically correct for each adopted model.
Replacement with true model-native fields where available.



A.4 Multi-Model Input Contract Is Rigid
Comparison artifacts assume a specific compares.qs structure (type, value, Year, source) and stop if it changes.
What is missing:

Adapter functions for alternate comparison formats.
Validation/reporting that degrades gracefully instead of hard-failing on schema changes.



A.5 Direct Source-File Dependency Persists In Narrative Chunks
Some narrative sections still pull values directly from source-run files instead of relying only on standardized ASAR artifacts.
What is missing:

A clean boundary where report rendering consumes only bridged outputs.
Reduced coupling to source-run directory layout for reproducibility and portability.
